# AP-BAG-001 Staff Baggage Handling and Escalation

## 1. Purpose and Scope  
This policy establishes the procedures and responsibilities for the handling of checked baggage throughout the airport's baggage handling system. It outlines the roles and responsibilities of staff involved in the movement and management of baggage, ensuring that all operations are conducted safely, efficiently, and in compliance with applicable regulations. The scope of this policy includes all baggage handling activities from the check-in belts through the baggage make-up area and onto the aircraft loading zones. It applies to all staff members assigned to baggage handling duties, including Baggage Handlers, Baggage Duty Supervisors, and Ramp Leads. This policy ensures consistency in operations and provides a framework for the escalation of incidents and the management of restricted items found in baggage.

## 2. Roles and Responsibilities  
The Baggage Handler is responsible for the safe and efficient movement of checked baggage between the check-in belts, the baggage make-up area, and the aircraft loading zones. This includes loading and unloading baggage, ensuring that all bags are properly secured, and maintaining the integrity of the baggage handling system. The Baggage Duty Supervisor oversees the operations of all Baggage Handlers and is responsible for monitoring the flow of baggage, ensuring compliance with safety and operational standards, and providing guidance and support to staff. The Ramp Lead is responsible for coordinating baggage handling activities with aircraft operations, ensuring that baggage is loaded and unloaded in accordance with flight schedules and safety protocols. All staff must adhere to this policy and report any deviations or incidents in accordance with established procedures.

## 3. Handling Standards  
All baggage must be handled with care to prevent damage, loss, or misrouting. Baggage Handlers must ensure that all bags are properly tagged, loaded, and secured during transit. Special attention must be given to heavy bags and fragile items, which require additional handling precautions to prevent injury or damage. Heavy bags must be loaded and unloaded using appropriate equipment and techniques to minimize the risk of strain or injury to staff. Fragile items must be clearly marked and handled with extra care to prevent breakage or damage. All baggage must be moved in a manner that maintains the integrity of the baggage handling system and ensures the timely delivery of luggage to its intended destination. Staff are required to maintain a high standard of professionalism and attention to detail throughout all stages of baggage handling.

## 4. Baggage Incident Escalation  
When a baggage handler finds a damaged, leaking, or unattended checked bag in the baggage make-up area, the handler must escalate the incident to the Baggage Duty Supervisor within 10 minutes of discovery and must report it under AP-INC-002. All baggage incidents, including but not limited to damaged, leaking, or unattended bags, must be documented and reported in accordance with the procedures outlined in AP-INC-002. The Baggage Duty Supervisor is responsible for assessing the incident, determining the appropriate course of action, and ensuring that all relevant parties are informed. In the event of a serious incident, such as a fire, explosion, or hazardous material spill, the Baggage Duty Supervisor must immediately notify the appropriate emergency services and follow the procedures outlined in the airport's emergency response plan. All staff must be trained to recognize and respond to baggage incidents in a timely and effective manner.

## 5. Restricted Items Found in Baggage  
If a restricted item is found in a bag during baggage handling, the bag must not be further processed until it is either approved or removed under the restricted-items approval procedure in AP-SEC-003. The Baggage Duty Supervisor is responsible for ensuring that all restricted items are properly identified, isolated, and reported in accordance with the procedures outlined in AP-SEC-003. Staff must not attempt to handle or transport a bag containing a restricted item without first obtaining approval from the relevant authority. All bags containing restricted items must be clearly marked and stored in a secure location until the appropriate action is taken. The Ramp Lead is responsible for coordinating the removal or handling of such bags in accordance with the airport's security protocols and ensuring that all relevant parties are informed of the situation.

## 6. Records and Review  
All baggage incidents and restricted item findings must be recorded in an incident log maintained by the Baggage Duty Supervisor. The incident log must include details such as the date and time of the incident, the location, a description of the incident, and the actions taken. This log is used for internal review, training, and continuous improvement of baggage handling procedures. The policy must be reviewed annually by the Baggage Duty Supervisor and approved by the appropriate management to ensure its continued relevance and effectiveness. All staff must be made aware of any changes to the policy and trained accordingly. The annual review process ensures that the policy remains aligned with current operational standards, regulatory requirements, and best practices in baggage handling.
